problems.title: 1's Complement Subtraction (M >= N)
problems.description: Subtract 1001 (9) from 1100 (12) using 1's complement.
problems.code:
M = 1100, N = 1001
1's complement of N (1001) = 0110
Add M and 1's complement of N:
  1100
+ 0110
------
 10010
An end-around carry occurs. Add the carry to LSB:
  0010
+    1
------
  0011 (Decimal 3)

problems.title: 1's Complement Subtraction (M < N)
problems.description: Subtract 1100 (12) from 1001 (9) using 1's complement.
problems.code:
M = 1001, N = 1100
1's complement of N (1100) = 0011
Add M and 1's complement of N:
  1001
+ 0011
------
  1100
No end-around carry. Take 1's complement of the result and attach a negative sign:
Result = -(1's complement of 1100) = -0011

problems.title: 2's Complement Subtraction (M >= N)
problems.description: Subtract 1010 (10) from 1101 (13) using 2's complement.
problems.code:
M = 1101, N = 1010
2's complement of N (1010) = 0101 + 1 = 0110
Add M and 2's complement of N:
  1101
+ 0110
------
 10011
An end carry occurs. Discard the carry:
Result: 0011 (Decimal 3)

problems.title: 2's Complement Subtraction (M < N)
problems.description: Subtract 1101 (13) from 1010 (10) using 2's complement.
problems.code:
M = 1010, N = 1101
2's complement of N (1101) = 0010 + 1 = 0011
Add M and 2's complement of N:
  1010
+ 0011
------
  1101
No carry occurs. Take the 2's complement of the result and attach a negative sign:
Result = -(2's complement of 1101) = -(0010 + 1) = -0011

problems.title: Canonical SOP Conversion
problems.description: Convert the standard SOP function F(A, B, C) = AB + C' into its Canonical SOP form.
problems.code:
Identify missing variables in each term:
Term 1: AB (missing C) -> AB(C + C') = ABC + ABC'
Term 2: C' (missing A and B) -> (A + A')(B + B')C' = ABC' + AB'C' + A'BC' + A'B'C'
Combine terms and remove duplicates:
F(A, B, C) = ABC + ABC' + AB'C' + A'BC' + A'B'C'

problems.title: K-Map Simplification
problems.description: Simplify the Boolean function F(A, B, C, D) = Σm(0, 1, 2, 5, 8, 9, 10) using a 4-variable K-map.
problems.code:
Plot the 1s on a 4-variable map:
Group 1 (Quad at corners: m0, m2, m8, m10) -> B'D'
Group 2 (Quad: m0, m1, m8, m9) -> C'D'
Group 3 (Pair: m1, m5) -> A'C'D
Simplified expression: F = B'D' + C'D' + A'C'D

problems.title: AND Gate using NAND
problems.description: Implement an AND gate using only 2-input NAND gates.
problems.code:
NAND gate output = (A * B)'
Invert the NAND output using a second NAND gate configured as a NOT gate:
AND = ((A * B)')' = A * B
Total NAND gates required: 2

problems.title: OR Gate using NAND
problems.description: Implement an OR gate using only 2-input NAND gates.
problems.code:
By DeMorgan's Theorem, A + B = (A' * B')'
Step 1: Invert A using a NAND gate -> A'
Step 2: Invert B using a NAND gate -> B'
Step 3: Feed A' and B' into a third NAND gate -> (A' * B')' = A + B
Total NAND gates required: 3

problems.title: NOT Gate using NAND
problems.description: Implement a NOT gate using only a 2-input NAND gate.
problems.code:
Tie both inputs of a NAND gate together:
Input = A
Output = (A * A)' = A'
Total NAND gates required: 1

problems.title: NOR Gate using NAND
problems.description: Implement a NOR gate using only 2-input NAND gates.
problems.code:
NOR output = (A + B)'
Step 1: Implement an OR gate using 3 NAND gates -> (A + B)
Step 2: Invert the OR output using a 4th NAND gate -> (A + B)'
Total NAND gates required: 4

problems.title: NAND Gate using NOR
problems.description: Implement a NAND gate using only 2-input NOR gates.
problems.code:
NAND output = (A * B)' = A' + B'
Step 1: Invert A using a NOR gate -> A'
Step 2: Invert B using a NOR gate -> B'
Step 3: Feed A' and B' into a third NOR gate -> (A' + B')' = A * B
Step 4: Invert that output using a 4th NOR gate -> (A * B)'
Total NOR gates required: 4

problems.title: Binary to Gray Code Conversion
problems.description: Convert the binary number 1101 to Gray code.
problems.code:
Binary: B3 B2 B1 B0 = 1 1 0 1
Gray: G3 G2 G1 G0
G3 = B3 = 1
G2 = B3 XOR B2 = 1 XOR 1 = 0
G1 = B2 XOR B1 = 1 XOR 0 = 1
G0 = B1 XOR B0 = 0 XOR 1 = 1
Result: 1011_Gray

problems.title: Gray to Binary Code Conversion
problems.description: Convert the Gray code 1011 to its binary equivalent.
problems.code:
Gray: G3 G2 G1 G0 = 1 0 1 1
Binary: B3 B2 B1 B0
B3 = G3 = 1
B2 = B3 XOR G2 = 1 XOR 0 = 1
B1 = B2 XOR G1 = 1 XOR 1 = 0
B0 = B1 XOR G0 = 0 XOR 1 = 1
Result: 1101_Binary

problems.title: Full Adder Logic Equations

problems.code:

Sum (S) = A XOR B XOR Cin
Carry-out (Cout) = AB + BCin + ACin
problems.output: S = A ^ B ^ Cin, Cout = AB + BCin + ACin

problems.title: Full Subtractor Logic Equations

problems.code:

Difference (D) = A XOR B XOR Bin
Borrow-out (Bout) = A'B + BBin + A'Bin
problems.output: D = A ^ B ^ Bin, Bout = A'B + BBin + A'Bin

problems.title: Decade Counter Specifications
problems.description: Identify the MOD number, number of flip-flops needed, and the maximum count state of a Decade Counter.
problems.code:
Decade Counter (MOD-10 Counter):
MOD number = 10 (counts 10 states: 0 to 9)
Number of flip-flops (n): 2^(n-1) < 10 <= 2^n -> n = 4 flip-flops
Maximum count state = 9 (1001 in binary)

problems.title: Synchronous Counter Design
problems.description: Determine the excitation table equations for designing a 2-bit Synchronous Up-Counter using T flip-flops (Q1 Q0).
problems.code:
Present State (Q1 Q0) -> Next State (Q1* Q0*):
00 -> 01 (T1=0, T0=1)
01 -> 10 (T1=1, T0=1)
10 -> 11 (T1=0, T0=1)
11 -> 00 (T1=1, T0=1)
Simplifying excitation inputs:
T0 = 1
T1 = Q0

problems.title: Asynchronous Counter Frequency
problems.description: A 4-bit Asynchronous ripple counter is supplied with an input clock frequency of 16 MHz. What is the output frequency of the last flip-flop (MSB)?
problems.code:
Number of flip-flops (n) = 4
Division factor = 2^n = 2^4 = 16
Output frequency (F_out) = F_in / Division factor
F_out = 16 MHz / 16 = 1 MHz

problems.title: RAM Chip Capacity Calculation
problems.description: How many 256 x 8 RAM chips are required to construct a 2K x 8 memory system?
problems.code:
Required Memory Depth = 2K = 2048 words
Chip Memory Depth = 256 words
Word size matches (8 bits)
Number of chips = Required Depth / Chip Depth
Number of chips = 2048 / 256 = 8 chips

problems.title: Address and Data Lines Calculation
problems.description: Find the number of address lines and data lines required for a 4K x 16 memory chip.
problems.code:
Memory Size = 4K x 16
Data lines = Word width = 16 lines
Address size = 4K = 4096 words
2^n = 4096 -> n = 12 address lines
